messages:
Maya: quick sync — Acme just escalated: competitor rolled out a 'multi-model routing' toggle they claim reduces cost by 30% for bursty chat. Sales asked if we can offer something similar by their renewal in 6 weeks.
Jonas: can you paste what exactly they want? is it a new API or just a config toggle?
Maya: Alex forwarded it — high level: automatic per-request routing to cheaper model variants, prefer low-latency paths for premium users, fallback to baseline. They want a self-serve toggle and SLA for pilot.
Alex (sales): renewal pressure: they want a concrete timeline. If we can promise a pilot within 6 weeks, they sign a 1yr Dedicated commit. If not, they lean to competitor.
Ciara: rough engineering ask: routing+policy layer + cheap-variant catalog + monitoring. MVP could be a config flag that toggles model selection logic per API key.
Sam (eng-lead): estimate MVP effort: 3 wks infra spike + 2 wks integration + 1 wk canary + QA = ~7 weeks (tight). If we do a compatibility shim (route on proxy) we can cut to ~4 wks but it’s brittle.
Maya: tradeoff: parity (shim) gets the deal now but increases maintenance debt; building a robust routing policy will be a differentiator for 2026. Recommend shim -> pilot -> parallel invest in proper routing. Thoughts?
Jonas: pragmatic: do shim with clear rollback and telemetry. Important to capture per-request chosen-variant, latency, token-cost. We should also gate by customer tier so default behavior unaffected.
Ciara: agree. Need launch acceptance criteria though. Suggest:
- median p99 delta latency vs baseline <= +50ms
- cost-per-request reduction >= 20% for routed traffic
- mismatch/regression rate (semantic quality) < 2% on our eval prompt set
- feature behind per-tenant opt-in flag
Maya: those look good. Add SLO: zero-severity data leaks and an audit log for chosen model variants.
Sam (eng-lead): ops note: must support automatic fallback if cheap variant hits OOM or latency spike. Plan to reuse existing fallback plumbing with a new "routing-policy" layer. Example minimal config:```json
{"policy": "prefer-cheap-if-latency-ok", "max_extra_latency_ms": 50, "variants": ["gpt-small-q4", "gpt-medium-q4", "redwood-base"]}```
Alex (sales): can we promise the audit + opt-in for pilot timeline? I need language for legal.
Jonas: audit logs are straightforward (we already log model id per request). Opt-in flag is trivial on the routing config.
Maya: OK decision: ship a compatibility shim behind tenant opt-in as pilot (target: pilot in 4 weeks). Parallelly kick a 6-week spike to design the full routing policy for Q2.
Ciara: action items:
- Jonas: implement shim + telemetry + opt-in (due in 3w)
- Sam: design canary + fallback runbook (due in 1w)
- Maya: coordinate pilot with Alex, draft customer-facing pilot docs & legal ask (due 5d)
- Dev-bot: create tracking epic `#prod-epic/feature-hedge-routing`
Jonas: noted. I'll put up a short RFC with interface and telemetry events.
Alex (sales): I'll soft-sell the pilot and set renewal expectation that full platform routing is planned next quarter.
Maya: one more: keep signal hooks to Redwood Optimize so we can recommend quantization/variant choices automatically if customers want cost controls.
Sam (eng-lead): will include metrics so Optimize can consume them (token-cost, latency, accuracy proxy).
Maya: cool. If nobody objects, I'll mark this as agreed and update roadmap slack thread. :ok_hand:
Jonas: agree.
Ciara: agree.
Alex (sales): thumbs up.
Dev-bot: epic created: prod-epic/feature-hedge-routing (id: EPIC-8421)
